hints.title: Component Topology Decomposition
hints.text: Partition the graph into connected components, distinguishing simple cycles from simple paths.

hints.title: Greedy Weight Allocation
hints.text: Assign the largest available values to components that generate the highest multiplication density, prioritizing cycles over paths.

hints.title: Alternating Value Arrangement
hints.text: Arrange assigned values in an alternating snake order around the cycle or path to maximize adjacent products.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List
from collections import deque

class Solution:
    def maxScore(self, n: int, edges: List[List[int]]) -> int:
        graph = [[] for _ in range(n)]
        for u, v in edges:
            graph[u].append(v)
            graph[v].append(u)
        seen = [False] * n
        cycle_sizes = []
        path_sizes = []
        for i in range(n):
            if seen[i]:
                continue
            comp = [i]
            seen[i] = True
            for u in comp:
                for v in graph[u]:
                    if not seen[v]:
                        seen[v] = True
                        comp.append(v)
            if all(len(graph[u]) == 2 for u in comp):
                cycle_sizes.append(len(comp))
            elif len(comp) > 1:
                path_sizes.append(len(comp))

        ans = 0
        rem_n = n
        for sz in cycle_sizes:
            left, right = rem_n - sz + 1, rem_n
            w = deque([right, right])
            score = 0
            for val in range(right - 1, left - 1, -1):
                fv = w.popleft()
                score += fv * val
                w.append(val)
            ans += score + w[0] * w[1]
            rem_n -= sz

        for sz in path_sizes:
            left, right = rem_n - sz + 1, rem_n
            w = deque([right, right])
            score = 0
            for val in range(right - 1, left - 1, -1):
                fv = w.popleft()
                score += fv * val
                w.append(val)
            ans += score
            rem_n -= sz
        return ans
```

complexity.notes: Linear time traversal and component sorting.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Trying all vertex permutations yields factorial complexity O(V!).
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Component size grouping allows immediate greedy arithmetic.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Differentiate cycle components from path components and demonstrate greedy optimality.
